content: The Value TB Costing Tool Suite includes a Data Collection Tool, which is highlighted in orange, and is designed to estimate the unit costs of tuberculosis (TB) services. This tool is used to collect data at the facility level, incorporating country-specific assumptions and parameters, as well as facility-specific TB service delivery outputs. The tool is complemented by Costing Guidelines for Tuberculosis Interventions, which provide a framework for facility provider cost analysis. The Data Collection Tool is structured to gather detailed information on facility characteristics, service outputs, and resource utilization. Data is entered into yellow-highlighted cells, while blue sheets capture facility-specific data such as service outputs, capital assets, building dimensions, and overhead costs. Green sheets are used to record prices for drugs, supplies, and equipment, while grey sheets focus on TB service utilization, including standardized service outputs, diagnostic tests, and drug regimens. Red sheets are dedicated to capturing staff time and resource usage, which are critical inputs for both top-down and bottom-up costing methodologies. The tool allows for the collection of data on the annual number of outpatient and community visits for TB-related services, as well as the total utilization of the facility. It also provides a breakdown of quantities relevant to top-down and bottom-up costing. For example, top-down quantities for drugs refer to the total amount of each TB medication disbursed at the facility, while bottom-up quantities are based on sampled usage by individual patients. Staff time is captured using two methods: interviews and weekly timesheet templates. These templates can be printed or provided electronically to staff members at the beginning of the data collection week and collected at the end. Total drug expenditure is estimated using the product of the total annual quantity of drugs disbursed and their unit prices. Bottom-up calculations are performed by multiplying drug prices by the average quantity used per patient for each TB treatment and prevention regimen. The Data Collection Tool is closely linked to the Data Entry Tool, where collected data is transferred for cost allocation to departments and services, and unit costs are calculated. If a cell in the tool is not applicable, it can be left blank or marked green, but entering NA or 0 is discouraged as it may affect calculations. The tool is adaptable to specific contexts, allowing users to add country-appropriate service outputs, drug names, test procedures, and other relevant labels. It includes optional sheets for planning data collection, such as identifying contact persons for each TB intervention type while ensuring data protection and anonymity. The estimated time for data collection varies by facility type, ranging from two days for a health center to two weeks for a regional hospital or reference laboratory. The tool also includes a checklist to track data collection progress, with color-coded status indicators for not started, in progress, completed, and not applicable. This checklist helps organize the costing process and ensures comprehensive data collection. Facility characteristics, such as location, size, operating hours, and staff composition, are recorded to provide context for the analysis. The tool captures information on the geography of the facility, including whether it is located in an urban or rural area, and the socio-economic status of the community it serves. The size of the facility's buildings and land is also reported. The Value TB project, funded by the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, aims to work with National Tuberculosis Programmes (NTPs) in high TB burden countries to collect unit cost data using standardized methods. The project focuses on TB interventions relevant for local planning and resource projection. The Data Collection Tool is designed to estimate the economic and financial costs of TB services from the provider's perspective, using both bottom-up and top-down approaches. Data collection typically takes one week per facility and involves 20 to 30 public and private TB service providers nationally. The tool includes instructions for its use, with color-coded sheets and cells to guide data entry. Black sheets are for study planning, blue sheets capture facility data, grey sheets describe TB service delivery, green sheets record prices and expenditures, and red sheets focus on staff time. Optional sheets provide additional instructions and space for notes to explain data sources or calculation methods. Yellow cells are designated for data input, while blue text provides guidance throughout the tool. Facility-level data collection begins with a meeting with the facility manager to outline the objectives of the Value TB project and obtain informed consent. An overview of the facility's characteristics and the population it serves is then gathered. This information is used to describe the facility and provide context for reporting results.
